question:
A 53-year-old previously healthy male presents with fever, severe headache, myalgias, and loose
stools that started one day ago. These symptoms began 10 days after returning from Mumbai, India.
His vital signs show: temperature 38.9°C, heart rate 117/min, blood pressure 108/80 mm Hg,
respiratory rate 25/min, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. His Covid-19 vaccinations are current,
and SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. Laboratory results show: | | Patient value | Reference range | | ---
| --- | --- | | Leukocyte count (per mm3) | 4200 | 4500–11,000 | | Hemoglobin (g/dL) | 11.4 | 13.5–17.5 | |
Platelet count (per mm3) | 110,000 | 150,000–350,000 | | Aspartate aminotransferase (U/liter) | 77 |
0–35 | | Alanine aminotransferase (U/liter) | 85 | 0–35 | | Lactate dehydrogenase (U/liter) | 285 |
100–190 | | Indirect bilirubin (mg/dL) | 0.4 | 0.1–0.3 | His creatinine and cerebrospinal fluid analysis are
normal. Initial thick and thin smears are negative for malaria. Blood cultures are pending. Chest
radiograph reveals a mild diffuse interstitial pattern. After hospital admission and initiation of empiric
ceftriaxone and azithromycin for presumed pneumonia, the patient reports worsening dyspnea,
headaches, and malaise at 12 hours. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Start empirical treatment for leptospirosis (B) Order serological testing for dengue
fever (C) Perform a computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest to evaluate for pulmonary embolism
(D) Order a stool culture to evaluate for enteric bacterial pathogens (E) Repeat thick and thin smears
for malaria (F) Order polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing for chikungunya virus (G) Start
intravenous corticosteroids for suspected autoimmune disease (H) Perform a lumbar puncture to rule
out meningitis (I) Initiate empiric treatment for typhoid fever (J) Order serological testing for yellow fever
 A. Order a stool culture to evaluate for enteric bacterial pathogens

B. Order serological testing for yellow fever
C. Order polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing for chikungunya virus
D. Start empirical treatment for leptospirosis
E. Start intravenous corticosteroids for suspected autoimmune disease
F. Repeat thick and thin smears for malaria
G. Perform a computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest to evaluate for pulmonary embolism
H. Order serological testing for dengue fever
I. Perform a lumbar puncture to rule out meningitis
J. Initiate empiric treatment for typhoid fever
